gloss: beginning of spring; first day of spring

definitions.gloss: beginning of spring; first day of spring (in the traditional calendar)
definitions.explanation: One of the 24 solar terms in the traditional East Asian calendar, marking the start of spring. Falls around February 3-5 in the modern calendar. Despite the name, it is still cold in most of Japan at this time.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{立春|りっしゅん}です。
examples.english: Today is the first day of spring.

examples.japanese: {立春|りっしゅん}を{過|す}ぎても{寒|さむ}い{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}く。
examples.english: Cold days continue even after the start of spring.

examples.japanese: {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では{立春|りっしゅん}だが、まだまだ{冬|ふゆ}の{寒|さむ}さが{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: On the calendar it's the start of spring, but the winter cold still lingers.

notes:
Composed of {立|りつ} (stand/establish) and {春|しゅん} (spring). One of the {二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき} (24 solar terms), an ancient system dividing the year based on the sun's position. {立春|りっしゅん} typically falls around February 4th.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立春|りっしゅん}を{迎|むか}える: to welcome the start of spring
- {立春|りっしゅん}{大吉|だいきち}: great luck on the first day of spring (auspicious phrase)
- {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では{立春|りっしゅん}: on the calendar it's spring

CULTURAL NOTE:
The day before {立春|りっしゅん} is {節分|せつぶん}, when people throw beans ({豆|まめ}まき) to drive away evil spirits. Letters written after {立春|りっしゅん} conventionally use spring greetings even if the weather is still cold.

RELATED WORDS:
- {立夏|りっか}: beginning of summer
- {立秋|りっしゅう}: beginning of autumn
- {立冬|りっとう}: beginning of winter
- {節分|せつぶん}: the day before {立春|りっしゅん}, bean-throwing festival
